governing_question: Does Echo already contain most components necessary for a coherent adaptive cognitive loop, with the primary limitation being insufficient connection between them?
method: Live source tracing (grep/read of actual runtime code, not documentation), live data reads (memory/river_brain.pkl unpickle, memory/council_cursor.json, memory/shadow_self_model.json, memory/self_model.json, memory/shadow_accuracy.jsonl, memory/SELF_EDIT.log, app/core/self_edit_convergence.json, data/question_garden.jsonl, sandbox/echo_projects/*/_report.md, memory/interaction_log.jsonl line count), and reads of prior forensic audits (2026-09-02 gap analysis, 2026-09-02 information-flow-integrity implementation, prior capability-ceiling map). No code was modified. No P1/P1.2/Learning-Pilot/P2/P3/C1 evidence touched.

edges.evidence: 13,417 real entries confirmed live. 7,788 (58%) carry parent_questions, 5,615 (42%) carry children -- real, non-trivial lineage accumulation, not just schema presence.
Live memory/echo_projects_autonomy_state.json confirms spec_source='garden' -- a real garden question genuinely became a real autonomous build spec.

edges.edge: question/spec -> goal object with identity/lineage that survives restart and competes with other goals
edges.evidence: echo_projects_autonomy_state.json's real schema is exactly {last_run_utc, last_status, spec_source} -- no goal ID, no priority, no competing-goals structure, no resumption pointer. A garden question is picked fresh each 6h cycle with no memory of a prior cycle's specific goal. question_garden's lineage fields (parent_questions/children) are a real relationship graph between QUESTIONS, not a goal-tracking/competition/resumption structure.

Real council deliberation genuinely produces a structured file list; confirmed live via a real 6-file autonomous cycle. Plan carries no persistent goal identifier forward beyond the one report file it's embedded in -- no goal_id/plan_id cross-reference schema exists.

QUANTIFIED LIVE: 61 real project directories exist. Only 13/61 (21%) ever reached the F2 (multi-file import+run) stage at all -- 48/61 (79%) were blocked at F1 before any execution was attempted. Of the 13 that reached F2, 13/13 (100%) show F2 status = FAIL. Net: 0/61 (0%) real cycles have ever produced a project that passed both F1 and F2.

edges.source: F1/F2 results, self-edit sandbox results, code_verification.py
edges.destination: a pass/fail verdict, independent of the generator
edges.mechanism: F1 static AST scan, F2 kernel sandbox-exec, code_verification.py's real sandboxed re-execution of claimed examples
edges.evidence: Verification is genuinely independent (real kernel sandbox, not a self-report) and CAN and DOES reject success -- confirmed via a live SELF_EDIT.log tail showing real, current safety_blocked/staging_import_failed rejections this session, and echo_projects' own 100% F2-fail rate among the 13 that reached it.

edges.destination: reflection text (either reflection_shard.jsonl's structured self-edit entries, or reflection_shard.py's generative musings)
edges.mechanism: TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS, must not be conflated
edges.evidence: (A) self_edit_manager.py's save_reflection() writes STRUCTURED entries into reflection_shard.jsonl carrying real result/quality-delta fields whenever a self-edit cycle reaches a terminal state -- this IS real outcome data reaching a reflection log. (B) reflection_shard.py's own generative _generate_reflection()/_generate_meta_reflection() (the 'ReflectionShardAutonomy' free-association loop) reads ONLY a signal string + past reflection embeddings -- confirmed by direct source read to contain NO reference to verification/outcome/quality data of any kind. Do not treat (B) as 'verification reaching reflection' -- it does not.

Live self_model.json confirms a real, well-evidenced target: targets={'next_self_edit_focus':'coding','reason':'avg_quality=2.37 (threshold=2.5), obs=99027'} -- derived from real RiverBrain observation counts and real recent quality averages, not a placeholder.

edges.edge: self-model targets -> actual self-edit targeting decision
edges.destination: perform_self_edit()'s target_task_type used for the real next cycle
edges.evidence: CRITICAL FINDING: perform_self_edit() checks memory/shadow_self_model.json FIRST as the 'highest-trust signal' and only falls back to SelfModelUpdater().get_weak_task_type() (which reads the real, well-evidenced self_model.json target above) if shadow_self_model.json has no focus set. In live practice shadow_self_model.json almost always HAS a focus set (see next edge), so the real, 99,027-observation-backed signal is demoted to a fallback that may rarely fire.

edges.edge: generative reflection text -> shadow_self_model.json override (metacognition edge)
edges.mechanism: shadow_model.propose_from_reflection(reflection_text), called from app/emergent_scheduler.py:723-724 on every real reflection cycle
edges.evidence: propose_from_reflection() is a PURE KEYWORD-COUNT HEURISTIC (4 task types x 5-6 keywords each), no LLM call, threshold >=2 keyword hits. LIVE DATA: shadow_accuracy.jsonl's last 15 hourly comparisons show shadow != real focus in 12/15 (80%) of readings -- the keyword heuristic overwhelmingly disagrees with the real, RiverBrain-performance-derived signal, which stayed 'coding' throughout. CAUSAL EFFECT DEMONSTRATED, NOT JUST INFERRED: a real self-edit cycle at 2026-09-03T21:38:26 targeted 'personal' -- the only deviation from 'coding' in the entire recent SELF_EDIT.log sample -- correlating exactly with shadow_self_model.json's own contemporaneous 'personal' proposal. This is a real, live, causally verified override of a well-evidenced signal by a low-information heuristic.
edges.confidence: high -- both the mechanism and one concrete instance of its real-world effect were directly confirmed

edges.source: quality_score computed on real generations (coding, self_edit_coding, echo_projects_coding buckets)
edges.evidence: Live unpickle of memory/river_brain.pkl: 9 real models x 7 real task-type buckets, richly populated (e.g. echo:latest/coding n=48,829, qwen2.5-coder:7b/coding mean=0.657, now the real leader among well-sampled models -- confirms Finding 39's tag-boost mechanism is empirically working). This is ROUTING-LEVEL learning (which model answers), not content-level.

edges.edge: council rating (peer-model quality judgment) -> RiverBrain blended training signal
edges.evidence: STRUCTURALLY REAL AND CORRECTLY GATED: is_council_trusted() live-confirmed True. learn_from_council_rating() is genuinely defined and genuinely called from rate_one_entry() when trust is True -- the code path is NOT dead in the source-code sense. BUT FUNCTIONALLY DEAD: memory/council_cursor.json reads {'position': 33471, 'updated_utc': '2026-07-26T14:15:33Z'} while memory/interaction_log.jsonl currently has only 11,671 real lines -- cursor position (33471) exceeds the file's current line count by 21,800. rate_one_entry()'s `new_lines = lines[cursor:]` on a shorter list returns an EMPTY LIST every single time (Python slicing past list length silently returns [] with no exception), so no new entry has been sampled/rated since approximately 2026-07-26. council_ratings.jsonl confirms this: 133 total lines, none newer than late July, despite 40+ days of continuous production interaction_log growth since. This CORRECTS the vague 'confirmed dead' claim in the prior capability-ceiling map (echo_capability_ceiling_map.json's learning_l2_autonomous dimension) with a precise, verified root cause: not a design flaw, a stale cursor left behind by an interaction_log rotation/reset event that never resynced this specific cursor.

edges.edge: self-edit outcome -> non_convergent_streak -> next self-edit prompt's Focus text (failure->adjustment)
edges.evidence: The mechanism and schema are real (self_edit_convergence.json exists with per-family cycles_attempted/non_convergent_streak fields; two entire families -- prose_stripping and quality_scoring -- were historically retired via this exact mechanism per project history). LIVE STATE: all 4 current families (prose_stripping, response_shortening, quality_scoring, unclassified) read non_convergent_streak=0 right now, despite a live SELF_EDIT.log tail this session showing many consecutive real staging_import_failed/safety_blocked results. This suggests the streak-reset condition (likely: reaching dry_run_staged resets the streak) fires even when a candidate never reaches real production deployment -- meaning the streak may rarely accumulate in current practice even amid frequent real failures. Not fully traced to a definitive root cause in this pass -- flagged as ambiguous, not concluded either way.
edges.confidence: medium -- the live zero-streak state is confirmed; the exact reason it stays at zero despite nearby failures is not fully traced

edges.edge: ToolManager registry -> tool name listing in system prompt
edges.evidence: list_tools() IS real and IS injected into the model's system prompt for TOOL_AWARE_TASKS or content-triggered cases -- this is not fully hollow. The model genuinely sees a real list of tool names.

edges.edge: model's tool-use intention -> actual tool invocation
edges.source: a model response naming/requesting a tool
edges.destination: ToolManager.get_tool(name) -> tool execution -> result fed back to the model
edges.evidence: grep -rn 'get_tool(' across the entire live codebase finds exactly one hit: the method's own definition in tool_manager.py. Zero real call sites anywhere -- not in Flask routes, not in council/river_deliberation.py, not in any autonomous loop, not in echo_model_orchestrator.py past the listing site. A fully-built registration+listing infrastructure with a completely absent invocation path. This is confirmed, not merely suspected, going beyond a simple grep as the mission requested: instantiation sites (2, both traced and read in full), decorators (the @tool-registration decorator in awareness_tools_integration.py only feeds discovery, not dispatch), dynamic lookup (none found), Flask endpoints (none found routing to get_tool), background loops (none call it).

edges.edge: memory retrieval (FAISS) -> generation content on the personal task path
edges.evidence: Write and read both real and live (123k+ vectors, correctly excluded from contamination categories). Finding 76's real 30-prompt ablation experiment (real vs. retrieval-disabled, same prompts) found the embedding-distance effect indistinguishable from ordinary sampling noise (p=0.48/0.37) -- retrieval technically occurs and is technically exposed to the model, but its measurable effect on the ONE task type tested (personal) could not be distinguished from chance.
edges.confidence: high (for the personal-task, temp>0 case specifically) -- explicitly UNKNOWN for other task types or temp=0

edges.evidence: CORRECTION to the prior capability-ceiling map, which stated 'no request-scoped correlation ID exists anywhere' -- that claim is now stale. A real trace_id mechanism exists, generated per Echo-Studio request and threaded through the council-deliberation and interaction-log write paths, explicitly built to fix the exact verification-ordering bug the 2026-09-02 gap analysis found (7 real unflagged fabrications). CORRECTION to the prior capability-ceiling map's 'top intervention #3' (thread caveat into interaction_log) -- this has ALREADY BEEN IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED per audits/2026-09-02_information_flow_integrity.md, which reports 2 live, unmocked reproductions post-fix showing the caveat and a matching trace_id in every persisted record, correcting a prior state where verification ran after the log-writing calls had already fired on the pre-verification draft.
edges.confidence: high -- per the source document's own two independent live reproductions

This is explicitly ROUTING-level adaptation, not content-level learning.

This is the cleanest possible real-world example of a 'stale cursor' failure mode: not a design flaw, a state-desync bug.

But the loop terminates at verification: 0/61 real historical cycles have ever passed both F1 and F2, and no downstream edge exists that feeds a verification failure back into how the NEXT cycle's question is chosen, planned, or generated -- echo_projects_autonomy_state.json's schema has no failure counter, no strategy field, nothing analogous to self_edit_convergence.json's non_convergent_streak. Each cycle is fully independent of every prior cycle's outcome.

closed_loops.status: CLOSED BUT BEHAVIORAL EFFECT PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED

But the fitness gate's own quality metric (raw AST node count) is confirmed saturated at a perfect 4/4 for all 25 currently-retained deploys -- meaning 'passed the gate' and 'quality genuinely improved' are conflated in the 92% headline, and the gate currently cannot discriminate among its own retained population at all.

closed_loops.reasoning: Every mechanical step is real and live. Finding 76's real ablation experiment could not distinguish the behavioral effect of disabling retrieval from ordinary sampling noise on this specific task type. This is a genuine, still-open null result, not a confirmed absence of effect and not a confirmed presence of effect.

closed_loops.status: DOES NOT EXIST (past the listing stage)

minimum_viable_closed_loop_proposal.loop: Self-edit outcome -> reflection -> self-model target -> [fixed priority] -> self-edit targeting -> outcome -> verify improvement
minimum_viable_closed_loop_proposal.not_the_curiosity_to_execution_loop: The mission's own suggested MVP shape (curiosity -> goal -> plan -> execution -> verification -> reflection -> metacognition -> routing adjustment -> next attempt -> verification -> measurable change) was investigated directly via echo_projects, its most plausible existing substrate. It is NOT the best candidate: it has no goal-persistence structure, no failure->adjustment edge, and a 0/61 historical success rate. The self-edit loop, not explicitly named in the mission's own suggested shape, was found organically during this investigation to already satisfy nearly every requirement of that shape, with one identified, small, surgical defect (the shadow-override priority issue).

minimum_viable_closed_loop_proposal.note: Both changes are fixes to existing, already-wired mechanisms, not new architecture -- consistent with the mission's stated preference for existing mechanisms over new ones and 1-3 surgical changes over a rewrite.

falsification_evidence: echo_projects: 0/61 real historical cycles have ever passed both F1 and F2 -- direct evidence that local models may be too weak for genuinely reliable multi-file, cross-referencing code generation, independent of any architectural connectivity fix.

C1's own live validation (this project's own prior work) found only 75% compliance (n=4) even with a 100%-reliable architectural chain -- direct evidence that persistent state alone is not sufficient to guarantee adaptive behavioral change; the frozen-weight model's own stochastic compliance is a real, separate ceiling.

reflection_shard.py's generative reflections read only a signal string + past-reflection embeddings, with zero access to verification/outcome data -- confirming that at least one major 'reflection' mechanism in this codebase is closer to stylistic free-association than outcome-grounded introspection, exactly as the mission's adversarial hypothesis suggested it might be.

The 2026-09-03 measurability audit's own finding (cited, not re-derived here) that apparent curiosity-category drift resolves to scheduling/persona code rather than emergent interest directly supports the 'curiosity may be scheduling rather than intrinsic inquiry' falsification candidate.

No evidence was found in this pass that RiverBrain's routing-level tag-boost adaptation (Finding 39) has ever been measured against actual downstream OUTCOME QUALITY, only against WHICH MODEL gets selected -- 'routing adaptation may not improve outcomes' remains a live, unfalsified possibility, not refuted by this investigation.

self_edit_convergence.json's non_convergent_streak reads 0 for all 4 families despite a live log tail full of real, recent failures -- either the failure->adjustment mechanism is working correctly (streak genuinely resets whenever ANY candidate reaches staging) or it is quietly inert in current practice; this investigation could not fully resolve which, which is itself evidence the mechanism's real-world engagement rate may be lower than its mere existence implies.
explicit_non_claims: This investigation does not establish that fixing the two proposed surgical changes would produce measurable content-level learning -- both changes affect ROUTING/TARGETING, not what gets generated.

This investigation does not establish whether memory retrieval causally affects behavior on any task type other than personal (only n=1 has ever been tested, per the 2026-09-02 gap analysis's own naming).
This investigation does not establish the root cause of self_edit_convergence.json's currently-zero streaks despite nearby real failures -- flagged as ambiguous, not resolved.

This investigation does not establish that wiring a real ToolManager invocation path would produce any net capability gain for this system's real task mix -- only that the infrastructure to register/list tools exists and invocation does not.

This investigation does not establish whether echo_projects' 0/61 success rate reflects a fixable calibration issue (F1's static scanner being too strict, F2's kernel sandbox being too strict) or a genuine model-capability ceiling -- both remain plausible and were not distinguished.

This investigation does not re-verify the 2026-09-02 architectural self-knowledge document series in full depth -- only its existence and the information-flow-integrity document's headline conclusions were read.

This investigation does not claim RiverBrain's routing-level learning constitutes 'learning' in any content-level sense -- per the mission's own Hard Rule 6, it is reported strictly as routing adaptation throughout.
